summary: Alaska State Troopers posted three Fairbanks-area items late Tuesday: a North Pole driver arrested on a suspended-license charge, a Fairbanks driver summonsed over marijuana found at a traffic stop, and a hit-and-run at a Geist Road gas station in which no one has been named. Fairbanks Police recorded a harassment and trespass arrest on Oct. 26 behind a court case filed the next day, and the court's weekly report for Oct. 21 to 27 lists 48 new criminal cases at Fairbanks, one at Nenana, one at Delta Junction and none at Healy; three of the Fairbanks numbers had not appeared in this report before and one of them cannot be found in the state's online case database.

entries.title: Suspended-license arrest: James Carpentino
body: James Carpentino, 48, of North Pole, was arrested on a charge of driving while his license was canceled, suspended or revoked — driving while a criminal-offense license suspension is in force — recorded by troopers as a Class A misdemeanor.

Troopers say they stopped him for a moving violation on Oct. 27 at about 5:09 p.m., and that the investigation showed his license was actively suspended for a criminal offense and that he had a prior conviction for the same offense within the last 10 years. He was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.
Alaska State Troopers case AK26106550. No court case has been filed.

entries.title: Marijuana summons: Jeremyah Murphy
body: Jeremyah Murphy, 18, was issued a summons on a charge of misconduct involving a controlled substance in the sixth degree and released at the scene.

Troopers say they stopped the vehicle on Geist Road at about 8:05 p.m. on Oct. 27 because it had no illuminated rear license plate, detected the odor of marijuana, and that Murphy voluntarily provided several dispensary containers, one of which held a partly smoked blunt.
Alaska State Troopers case AK26106606. No charge class is recorded and no court case has been filed.

entries.title: Hit-and-run at a Fairbanks gas station
body: Troopers are investigating a hit-and-run collision at the Circle K at Geist Road and Fairbanks Street on Oct. 27 at about 3:30 p.m. No one has been arrested or charged.

Troopers say witnesses reported a white Toyota Tacoma backing into a parked vehicle and leaving without providing information to the owner, and that surveillance footage from the business matched the witness account.
Alaska State Troopers case AK26106583. Troopers ask anyone with information to call the Fairbanks post at 907-451-5100.

entries.title: Harassment and trespass arrest: Scott Glen Dayton
body: Scott Glen Dayton, 29, was arrested on charges recorded by police as harassment, a misdemeanor, and criminal trespass.
Fairbanks Police record the arrest at the 1300 block of South University Avenue on Oct. 26 at 11:12 p.m. Police case 26003289.
A court case was opened the next day, 4FA-26-02173CR, which records that no charging document has been filed yet and states no charge class. Arraignment is set for Nov. 3.

entries.title: DV assault charge: Nicolette Nicolai
body: Nicolette Nicolai is charged with assault in the fourth degree — recklessly causing injury to another person — a Class A misdemeanor recorded as domestic violence. The charge is dated Oct. 19 at Fairbanks.
The case was filed Oct. 21 and the court issued a warrant on Oct. 22 with bail of $250 cash performance, with the defendant not to be released until the court approves conditions. No hearing is set.
Case 4FA-26-02132CR.

entries.title: DUI charge: Anthony Morandi Sosa
body: Anthony Morandi Sosa is charged with driving under the influence — operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs — a Class A misdemeanor. The charge is dated Oct. 24 at North Pole and the court record lists a breath reading of .163.
The case was filed at the Fairbanks courthouse on Oct. 24 and he was released on Oct. 26 on standard conditions.
Case 4FA-26-02151CR; arraignment Oct. 30.

sources.label: Alaska Court System weekly charges report

entries.title: A third Fairbanks case number cannot be looked up online
body: A third criminal case number printed in the Alaska Court System's weekly charges report cannot be found in the state's public case database.

Case 4FA-26-02127CR, listed in the report as filed at the Fairbanks courthouse on Oct. 21 against Annette Keogh with no charging document filed, returns no records on a search by case number. The report that lists it was produced at 9 p.m. on Oct. 27.
Two other case numbers reported earlier this week, 4FA-26-02165CR and 4FA-26-02171CR, still cannot be found either. Both closed on Oct. 26 and both are printed again in the new report.
